maya: heads up - saw a small but persistent tail-latency regression on streaming responses after the kernel-selection change. 
maya: repro runs show 95th/99th up ~20-40ms on short-chat workloads when KV cache thrash happens.
maya: behavior looks like: batch formation waits for token-budget target, partial-decode gets deprioritized, kernel switch triggers eviction and next batch loses warm KV so slow token emit.
sam: ugh. do you have an experiment id / perf traces?
maya: yes, run id `exp/stream-kernsel-2026-03-17` - attaching the perfbot summary below.
perfbot: 
```
perfbot: experiment: exp/stream-kernsel-2026-03-17
perfbot: workload: short-chat (mean prompt 18 tokens, avg generation 24 tokens)
perfbot: config: continuous-batching v2, token_budget_target=12, early_send_threshold=0.45, kernel_pref=fast-attn
perfbot: median latency: 32ms -> unchanged
perfbot: p95: 118ms -> +22ms
perfbot: p99: 252ms -> +37ms
perfbot: kv-miss rate during tail: 18% -> up from 6%
perfbot: note: spike aligned with kernel handoff events and partial-decode preemption
```
toni: thanks. 2 quick ideas: drop token_budget_target for streaming flows and increase early_send_threshold so partial-decode flush happens earlier. also look at decoupling kernel selection from immediate eviction - maybe delay eviction until batch boundary.
ash: (that's me, ash) +1 to delaying eviction. we have a cheap flag to prefer sticky kernels for N minutes after warmup. could try 30s sticky.
sam: if we lower token_budget_target we might increase overall cost; need to measure tokens/sec uplift. also watch for increased tiny batches -> kernel churn.
maya: agreed. propose A/B test: (A) token_budget_target=8 + early_send=0.6 + kernel_sticky=30s; (B) token_budget_target=12 + early_send=0.6 + delayed_eviction=on. measure p99, throughput, unit-cost.
toni: can we add a microtrace to partial-decode queue so we can see preemptions per request? right now we only see aggregate decode preemption counts.
maya: yes i'll add a short log with tags: `partial_decode_preempt=true/false`, `preempt_reason`, `kv_warm=false/true`, `kernel_switch=none|soft|hard`. output as condensed CSV to perf sink.
perfbot: scheduled: perf job exp/stream-kernsel-2026-03-18-A and -B, start 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC.
ash: quick note on kernel selection heuristics - current rule picks kernel based on expected seq_len and batching potential. that puts short-chats on small-kernel which is fast for median but more sensitive to KV misses. we could bias kernel selection toward KV-friendly kernels when workload is streaming (has KV usage).
sam: good point. maybe add a small cost function: score = latency_est + alpha * kv_miss_penalty where alpha tuned by traffic class.
maya: ok action items:
- maya: add microtrace and tags (ETA 3h)
- sam: implement A/B config and cost-fn prototype (ETA EOD)
- ash: toggle sticky kernel experiment and delayed-eviction flag (ETA 1h)
- toni: run perf analyses and validate unit-cost impact (ETA after jobs finish)

maya: one more: we saw a weird case where partial-decode resend leads to duplicate KV prefetches - we'll gate prefetch by request id to dedupe. adding that to worklist.
ash: ack.
toni: cool. if A/B shows p99 improvement without >2% cost increase we ship as interim.
maya: agreed. i'll post back with initial microtrace dump when available. :eyes: 
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
